statements.quote: The study was not formally preregistered, so we state explicitly which decisions preceded the data and which did not, and we report a sensitivity analysis for every decision in the second class.
statements.locator: p. 3, Section 2.1.1, What was fixed in advance, and what was not

statements.quote: Fixed in a dated internal analysis plan written before the data were analyzed: the three-arm structure and its instructions; the primary endpoint (dependent vs. no-AI on Phase-2 reasoning quality); the direction of H1–H3; the covariate set for each model (baseline ability plus same-phase time on task); the decision not to condition the primary transfer model on Phase-1 performance; the exclusion criteria of failed attention checks, missing Phase-2 data, long-string responding, and indications of AI use in the no-AI arm; the criteria used for that AI screening, which were written down before any essay was scored; and the family-wise treatment of the three objective outcomes under Benjamini–Hochberg correction.
statements.locator: p. 3, Section 2.1.1, dated internal analysis plan

statements.quote: A behavioral log recorded whether an outline was submitted first, the number of AI calls, the proportion of AI suggestions adopted vs. rewritten, and time on task; Section 3.1 reports these as the evidence that the manipulation was delivered.
The platform logged the full text of every prompt and every response, with timestamps.
statements.locator: p. 5, Section 2.5, The AI system, first paragraph

statements.quote: The complete Chinese instruction scripts, the system prompt, the prompt-template pool, the pinned model version with its sampling parameters, the three writing prompts, and the rating rubric are available from the corresponding authors upon reasonable request (see Data Availability).
statements.locator: p. 5, Section 2.5, The AI system, final paragraph

statements.quote: That is why the call-level record was logged and retained rather than the configuration alone. What participants actually saw is recoverable from those logs even when the model behind it is not.
statements.locator: pp. 5-6, Section 2.5, The AI system, final paragraph continued onto p. 6

statements.quote: The datasets analyzed for this study are not publicly available because they contain participant-level survey responses. De-identified data and analysis materials are available from the corresponding authors upon reasonable request, subject to institutional ethics requirements.

notes: Read the entire supplied markdown conversion (87,818 characters; 593 lines), including end matter and references, for the 15-page published paper. Verified the quoted passages against PDF text on pp. 3, 5-6, and 13; checked PDF link annotations and confirmed there are no embedded file attachments. The paper identifies one randomized experiment, S1, with Autonomous, Dependent, and No-AI arms. No public data, code, materials, preregistration, or supplementary-file URL is given in the availability passages; both data_url and code_url in forms/c463.json are null. The dated internal analysis plan is not a public preregistration. The publisher landing page and XML confirm the same availability restriction and reveal no separate supplement. The article's CC BY license does not establish a license for author-held data. No matching deposit was found in the recorded searches, so deposits is empty rather than treating the article itself or unrelated medical-search matches as data deposits. No participant data file could be inspected; participant identifiers, arm columns, outcome columns, raw participant essays, rows, and dataset license therefore remain unverified. The paper says prompt/response logs were retained, but this does not confirm that participant essays or logs would be supplied. The public sources do not enable computation of the missing S1 arm-level outcome means, SDs, or SEs identified in final.open_items, independent verification of analyzed counts or the 209-225 cell-range discrepancy, or diversity measures from participant texts. The classification rests on the explicit offer of de-identified data and analysis materials upon reasonable request, subject to institutional ethics requirements. No access request or author contact was made. OSF discovery was limited to the specified public-node title filter.
